📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few remnants of fashion history manage to stir up emotions and draw headlines quite like pieces from Alexander McQueen’s revered runways. Rare, technical, and sensorial, these are certainly not your average, everyday pieces of clothing. McQueen runway pieces are often flexed at the world’s top fashion exhibitions at museums around the world. That’s just one of the reasons why the multicolor silk minidress from Alexander McQueen spring/summer 2010 “Plato’s Atlantis” is the star of Christie’s December Luxury Week, where the runway gem will be hitting the auction block with a $150,000 to $300,000 estimate. The sale runs online from November 25 to December 10, 2026.

“Based on what we know about McQueen’s distribution at the time and the types of garments that went into production after a runway show, we estimate there were probably only fewer than two dozen examples of this exact dress produced,” Max Brownawell, head of handbags at Christie’s, tells ELLE. “Then on top of that, the importance of ‘Plato’s Atlantis,’ as McQueen’s final fully realized collection, really can’t be understated. He himself noted that his previous collection was his final as a young man. And so this was his most mature, fully fledged collection that he’d ever produced.”.

Industry observers note that the dress was the fourth look in the runway collection, styled with the iconic Armadillo boots. Designed with a futuristic sculpted drape, covered in prints from the natural world (think: a collage of abstracted imagery pulled from butterfly wings, snakeskin, and insects), the silhouette is a favorite of fashion fans and archivists. Brownawell shares that the piece still has the tag attached and has likely never been worn. The ensemble may very well exceed the estimate: for reference, a “Plato’s Atlantis” look complete with those aforementioned boots sold for $1.5 million including fees at a Fair Warning auction in New York on Sept. 17, 2026, setting an auction record for McQueen.

According to recent reports, “He was going for something that was entirely fresh,” says Brownawell. “This dress is a really prime example of that, the way that the print has been designed to lay perfectly within the architecture of the garment itself is really a spectacular sort of couture level of creation. On top of that, you have this unbelievably architectural draping, which, you know, McQueen has, it’s been said that he really actually draped a lot of these pieces directly onto the forms themselves because it was so complex.”.

Aside from the dress itself, Alexander McQueen’s spring/summer 2010 show was ahead of its time in every way. It was the first show to be livestreamed in real time on the internet, and it was the first fashion show to debut a major pop single during a show; Lady Gaga’s “Bad Romance” premiered during the show’s finale. “McQueen’s legacy has been just growing stronger and stronger every year,” adds Brownawell.

It has been revealed that the dress is hitting the auction block at a time when Christie’s is launching its inaugural fashion auction. “We really believe that the market is at a point right now where people do appreciate the important designs,” he states. “There’s a lot of clothing out there, but there’s also a lot of very important pieces that define what we wear and where fashion is going and where it’s been.”.

Breaking: Vogue’s Best Dressed People of 2026

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3696 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Our goal was 50—just 50!—of the best-dressed people of the year, a list to commemorate the unforgettable fashion moments of a very topsy-turvy 2026.
  • Recent findings suggest that we wanted them all, plus some highly fashionable characters from unexpected fields and walks of life, and we wanted couples, which we insisted should be counted as singletons (a technicality!).
  • Written by: Christian Allaire, Margaux Anbouba, Taylor Antrim, Max Berlinger, Laird Borrelli-Persson, Anna Cafolla, Liam Hess, Alexandra Hildreth, Hannah Jackson, Joan Kennedy, Irene Kim, Anna Grace Lee, Nicole Phelps, Madeleine Schulz, and Emma Specter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Our goal was 50—just 50!—of the best-dressed people of the year, a list to commemorate the unforgettable fashion moments of a very topsy-turvy 2026. Sounds easy…but, well, list-making never is. There were athletes who turned game days into runways, actors who owned the red carpet and the sidewalk, and method-dressing movie stars who artfully ignored the meaning of the word cut.

Recent findings suggest that we wanted them all, plus some highly fashionable characters from unexpected fields and walks of life, and we wanted couples, which we insisted should be counted as singletons (a technicality!). We struggled and horse-traded and voted and arrived finally at…55! (The same number as last year.) Here is the fruit of our labor: an unranked, diligently categorized, highly subjective list of Vogue’s best dressed of 2026. And it all begins with our cover star, a selection that was the result of a rather heated debate. Enjoy!

Written by: Christian Allaire, Margaux Anbouba, Taylor Antrim, Max Berlinger, Laird Borrelli-Persson, Anna Cafolla, Liam Hess, Alexandra Hildreth, Hannah Jackson, Joan Kennedy, Irene Kim, Anna Grace Lee, Nicole Phelps, Madeleine Schulz, and Emma Specter.

Vogue’s Best Dressed cover star is….

It has been revealed that STORRIE TIME Conner Storrie brings the Ken-ergy in a miniaturized version of his Gucci Best Dressed cover look. Coach watch pendant.

Sources indicate that why 2026 was his year: Playing brooding Russian hockey player Ilya Rozanov in the gay romance Heated Rivalry—in various states of deshabille—launched this 26-year-old Hollywood hopeful waiting tables in Los Angeles to cultural supernova. His last 12 months have seen a kind of fashion miracle: Storrie is now better known for what he wears than what he doesn’t. Click here for his cover-story conversation with Chloe Malle—which ranged from Storrie’s punk roots to his adoration of Parker Posey, his side hustle in “provocateur” photography, and more.

Friends, lovers, collaborators—occasionally all at once.

Spector and Hall wear Tom Ford.

Why 2026 was their year: Him: Train Daddy in The Gilded Age; Her: Wicked stepmother in Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story (and more).

Their couple style, in essence: Hudson Valley cabincore meets Tom Ford heat.

Kravitz wears The Row. Styles wears The Row and Adidas.

Their year in fashion: Excellent outerwear, statement headgear, rave-ready sunglasses, plenty of The Row.

In a recent development, their couple style, in essence: Kiss all the time. Dress alike, more than occasionally.

From left: Imhof wears Balenciaga, Teuscher wears Rodarte; both wear Valentino.

Why 2026 was their year: Teuscher traded Lincoln Center for Hong Kong to star in her partner Imhof’s queer, Shakespearean House of Swans.

Their couple style, in essence: Berghain Romeo and Juliet.

Barone in Missoni; Skinner in ERL.

It has been revealed that why 2026 was their year: Barone released comedy special Galaxy Brain; Skinner got to work on Overcompensating season 2. Together: their riotous podcast, Ride, and Halloween domination.

Their couple style, in essence: Newport Beach heartthrobs, if they canvassed for Zohran.

According to recent reports, left: Both in Dior. Right: Arquette wears Circus of Magdela; Lean wears Giorgio Armani.

Why 2026 was their year: Lean bringing down the house at the VMAs, while writing duets with Arquette; the couple hard-launching at Dior Men’s spring 2027 show.

Their couple style, in essence: Shades of blue (or bleu).

Left: Rosalía in Stella McCartney. Right: Bahia wears Saint Laurent; Rosalía wears Vivienne Westwood.

Their year in fashion: Contrasting-yet-coordinated masc-for-femme dressing, conjuring early days Justin and Hailey.

Why we can’t get enough: Two words: tooth necklace.

Johnson wears a Nour Hammour coat.

He stated; she said: MGK to Vogue: “I started kind of respecting my upkeep, and I’ve watched things open up.” Johnson to Vogue: “[Musicians] like me, I don’t know what to say.”.

Their couple style, in essence: Hoodies, diamonds, beanies, grommets, lace, leather, fangs. Misery business.

LIFE IN PLASTIC, IT’S FANTASTIC! Master of the step-and-repeat, Kendall Jenner set the gold standard for polka-dots in her Valentino Academy Gala dress.

The category is: great gowns, beautiful gowns.

Jenner wears Armani; Alexander Calder earrings.

Her year in fashion: Winged Victory at the Met, snagging ultra-rare Calder earrings for her first Lido, spreading the gospel of The Row, and perfecting polka dots at the Academy Gala.

Why we can’t get enough: She wears clothes like it’s her job.

In a recent development, why 2026 was her year: Rose, Fatherland, and Project Hail Mary! (And, ahem, Digger.).

Highlight reel: Matières Fécales’ riff on the bar suit; Chanel’s riff on the hedgehog.

Her year in fashion: Dior standouts (acid green Poiret punk and impressionistic water lilies, specifically), plus an Issey Miyake breastplate, Marc Jacobs sequins, and Lii color blocking.

Best look of 2026: That star-spangled scarlet High Sport halter dress with a swishy fringed hem for the London premiere of Toy Story 5—a clever, playful wink to the film’s universe that still felt fashion.

Mulligan wears (from left): Colleen Allen; Dries Van Noten; The Row; Celine.

Why 2026 was her year: Lending her voice to Wildwood, scoring an Emmy nom for Beef season 2, getting a CBE from the King (she wore The Row).

In a recent development, best look: That triptych of pixelated floral brocades from Julian Klausner’s fall 2026 Dries Van Noten collection. Bonus points for the pockets in the top!

Why this was her year: An awards-season run for Hamnet; an ultra-chic stint on the jury at Cannes.

Best look of 2026: Schiaparelli’s spiky “Isabella Blowfish” dress was a creepy-cheeky wow on the runway—and doubly satisfying on the Croisette.

It has been revealed that A DOLL’S HOUSE Who states you can only wear your Met Gala dress once? Back in her Barbie Dreamhouse closet, Paloma Elsesser plays dress-up in her bespoke Bureau of Imagination gown.

They’re wearing your favorite brand—you just don’t know it yet.

Elsesser wears (from left): Junya Watanabe; Comme des Garçons, Phoebe Philo shoes, Chanel bag; Goyagoma.

Why 2026 was her year: When she wasn’t on the hunt for her next vintage deep cut? Hitting the runway for Ferragamo and Junya Watanabe and debuting Francesco Risso’s Bureau of Imagination at the Met.

She’ll get bragging rights for: The Bureau of Imagination gown—patchworked, painted, and embellished by “a squadron of people.” A true one-of-a-kind.

Thompson wears Giovanna Flores; Kallmeyer.

Why 2026 was her year: A Golden Globes nomination for Hedda; the runaway thriller His & Hers; and her Broadway debut in Fear of 13 alongside Adrien Brody.

She’ll get bragging rights for: Her support of all things indie is as evident in her work as in her wardrobe: just take the enviably cool Giovanna Flores patchwork dress she wore on a sweltering day in Fresh York.

Peak wears (from left): Lii; Diotima; Torishéju.

Why 2026 was her year: She drummed up Hunger Games hype, toggling her looks between indie darlings and bona fide fashion-girl pulls.

She’ll get bragging rights for wearing: A scrunched-up black top and red cut-out leather skirt from London-based Torishéju; the standout textured Diotima dress from this season; and New York favorite Liii.

Ortega wears Pierre Cardin; Elias Matso.

She’ll get bragging rights for wearing: A custom dress from Polimoda fashion school graduate Elias Matso, made entirely from steel boning and beads in a process that took over 300 hours.

Her year in fashion: Ditching goth—at least until Wednesday season 3.

OUT OF THE BOX On the lively streets of Fresh York City, Sarah Pidgeon does her best CBK in a leopard-print Adam Lippes coat. Susan Alexandra pigeon charm.

Pigeon wears Chanel; Yohji Yamamoto.

Why 2026 was her year: She introduced a latest generation to Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy—and her Yohji Yamamoto-filled closet—in Love Story.

Give her an Oscar for this look: The lacy aqua blue slip dress she wore to the Chanel Pre-Oscars party married CBK-ish ’90s minimalism with present-day Blazy-mania.

Zendaya wears Matières Fécales.

Recent findings suggest that why 2026 was her year: The Drama! Spider-Man! The Odyssey! Dune! Oh, and she found time to marry Tom Holland, too.

Give her an Oscar for this look: The white strapless Matières Fécales gown with matching feathered wings while promoting The Odyssey was pure Athena realness.

Edgar-Jones wears (from left): Miu Miu; Andreas Kronthaler for Vivienne Westwood; Rodarte.

Why 2026 was her year: The 18th-century-inspired Sense and Sensibility press tour, featuring a dreamy blush Galliano jacket worn with jeans; sexed-up pantaloon sets from Dries Van Noten and Colleen Allen; and lots and lots of Stella McCartney-era Chloé.

Up next: Going toe-to-toe with Michelle Williams in A Place in Hell and bringing another book club favorite to the major screen in Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow.

Robbie wears Schiaparelli; Dilara Findikoglu.

Why we can’t get enough: Schiaparelli couture with Elizabeth Taylor’s legendary Taj Mahal diamonds one day, cutoff jorts the next.

Up Next: How will she method-dress for Untitled Ocean’s Eleven Prequel?

Fanning wears (from left): Robert Wun; Givenchy by Sarah Burton; Evan Clayton.

Why 2026 was her year: Earned her first Oscar nomination for Sentimental Value, delivered Margot’s Got Money Troubles, and dressed in her Capitol best for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

Her style, in essence: Anything can be a hat!

In a recent development, OFF THE SHELF Olivia Rodrigo, here in vintage Rudi Gernreich, brought major flower power with her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival. Susan Alexandra flower and mushroom charms.

Pop stars or politicians—they’re all headliners to us.

Rodrigo wears Versace; Hussein Chalayan.

Why 2026 was her year: It was a legacy-defining one between Rodrigo’s best album yet (hello, seven Grammy nominations) and her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields music festival, which raised $20 million to support nonprofits for women and girls.

Her year in fashion: She joined a long line of badasses who’ve subverted the babydoll dress—Kathleen Hanna and Courtney Love come to mind.

Michelle Obama wears Acne Studios.

It has been revealed that why we can’t get enough: From this summer’s ribbon-cutting at the Barack Obama Presidential Center in Thom Browne to attending the U.S. Open in red, white, and blue Chanel, she makes patriotism look chic.

The look that deserved a push notification: The Acne Studios skirt custom-printed with a photo of her late mother Marian Robinson, a gesture that brought the former president—and the rest of us—to tears.

Dion wears (from left): Tom Ford; Dior; Chanel; Chanel.

Why 2026 was their year: A triumphant return to the stage following her stiff person syndrome diagnosis meant 16 sold-out indicates at Paris’s Plénitude Arena, plus daily pap walks outside of Le Royal Monceau.

Recent findings suggest that the look that deserved a push notification: The custom Chanel sweetheart-neckline gown that took 1,380 hours to make—a recreation of her 1997 Oscars dress. Our hearts will go on!

Why 2026 was her year: Wrestling with mortality on Lost Weekend; stealing scenes in Primetime.

The look that deserved a push notification: In Venice, a lesson in indie-darling dressing: Gucci skirt suit, below-the-knee tattoo, visible leg hair.

Flanagan wears Sky-Eagle Collection.

Why 2026 was her year: The Minnesota senator-to-be’s midterm victory made her the first-ever Indigenous woman elected to the United States Senate.

The look that deserved a push notification: Victory called for a sleek burgundy suit and a traditional pair of dentalium shell earrings by Yurok artist Jessica Mendez.

According to recent reports, TINY FURNITURE Just like Mary, Cole Escola is the picture-perfect homemaker in the Christopher John Rogers jumpsuit they wore to the Tonys. Movado watch. Jennifer Behr earrings.

Imitation may be the sincerest form of flattery, but there’s no replicating one-of-one style.

Escola wears (from left): Chanel; Eckhaus Latta; vintage Eve Stillman.

Why 2026 was their year: Oh, Mary! went on the road, and Escola’s Miss Piggy became the in-the-works screenplay we didn’t know we needed.

Highlight reel: Coco cosplay at Chanel couture; an “ibuprofen”-pink Christopher John Rogers jumpsuit at the Tonys; an Eckhaus Latta deep cut at the CFDA Awards.

Taylor wears Schiaparelli; Thom Browne.

Why 2026 was her year: Who else could collect their Golden Globe in a bejeweled Schiaparelli whale tail?

Her best look: The trompe l’oeil Thom Browne at the SAG Awards, with her daughter Rue Rose on hand to adjust her train. As Taylor put it: “A very expensive stylist.”.

Why 2026 was his year: A longtime Comme des Garçons acolyte, Sedaris promoted his latest book, The Land and Its People, in layers of deconstructed tailoring, voluminous skirts, and oddball shoes.

Why we can’t get enough: Dressed in a diaphanous layered ensemble for Late Night With Seth Meyers, he quipped, “I think of this as a sports skirt.”.

Ellis Ross wears (from left): Prada; Balenciaga; Dries Van Noten.

Why this was her year: A Broadway debut in Every Brilliant Thing, an expanding Pattern Beauty lineup, a daytime Emmy for her show, Solo Traveling—and she found time to start styling herself.

Best look of 2026: That marigold Balenciaga at the 2026 Academy Museum Gala; beautifully textured, quintessentially her (with a dash of Law Roach).

Industry observers note that why we can’t get enough: What was the American Hagwon author’s first fashion flex when fiction started paying the bills? Early days Thom Browne. “I bought one of Thom’s first sweaters,” Lee told Vogue.

It has been revealed that best look of 2026: Her go-to matching pinstriped Comme des Garçons blazer and dress for large speaking events. Who mentioned a uniform can’t have style?

Hill wears (from left): Bottega Veneta; Saint Laurent; Balenciaga.

Why 2026 was her year: Became a BET Living Legend in voluminous, ruffled Saint Laurent with wrap-around sunglasses; reunited with Wyclef to celebrate the 30th anniversary of The Score; sat front row at Balenciaga spring 2027 as “Ready or Not” blared.

Her style in essence: Can’t take my eyes off you.

PAPER DOLL Audrey Nuna puts a bow on 2026 in the Thom Browne cape she wore to the Golden Globes.

You’ll never again have to ask, “Wait, where do I know them from?”.

Nuna wears Maison Margiela; Thom Browne.

Where you know her from: If you don’t know her face, odds are you’ve heard her sing: Nuna lent her voice to Mira in the Oscar- and Grammy-winning KPop Demon Hunters.

Best outfit of 2026: The cocoon-like black cape dress embellished with bows from Thom Browne—one of her more understated looks, if you can believe it.

You’ve heard them: Honking on their Getting Killed tour, SNL, or frontman Cameron Winter’s Carnegie Hall live album.

Industry observers note that their year in fashion: Well-worn band tees, threadbare tank tops, bug-eyed sunglasses, and dresses over jeans are par for the course. Their too-cool-for-school style is just that: too cool.

Lenae wears Natasha Zinko; Rabanne.

Why you should know her: The singer was marked safe from one-hit-wonderdom with her third album, Blue Island.

Best outfit of 2026: The eccentric, richly embellished Space Age Rabanne dress she wore to the Grammys was totally out of this world.

Where you know her from: Apple TV’s Shrinking and Kane Parsons’s instant horror classic Backrooms.

Sources indicate that best outfit of 2026: The peachy fall 2011 Prada minidress with rounded sleeves, sharp front pleats, and a belted drop waist that she wore during the Toronto International Film Festival. If Miuccia hasn’t already come calling…she should.

Sui Wonders wears Miss Sohee; Anna Sui.

Why you should know her: The actor—and niece of fashion designer Anna Sui—proved good taste is genetic while making the rounds for I Want Your Sex and The Studio.

Best outfit of 2026: At Sundance, she plumbed the family archives, settling on a funky, faux fur-trimmed slip dress and matching bonnet. She got it from her auntie!

Great on the red carpet; even better on a morning-after coffee run.

Lawrence wears (from left): Dior jacket, Completedworks earrings; The Row polo, Siedrés pants, Tory Burch necklace, The Row loafers; Junk Food T-shirt, Dries Van Noten skirt, Ancient Greek slippers, Hermès bag.

Her year in fashion: Vintage graphic tees; flowing trousers; boho scarves; slip-on Vans; oversized sunglasses; pendant necklaces; statement bags of the highest order.

Her style, in essence: Skate park chaperone.

Jacobson wears (from left): Khaite; Dilara Findikoglu; Mel Usine; Conner Ives.

Why we can’t get enough: The theatricality we want from a Yale Drama grad: high collars, slashed abs, daring necklines, sleek layering.

Industry observers note that on the clock: Her 2026 Met Gala look—as a Joan of Arc-esque figure in a coin-and-pin-adorned armored bodysuit by Dilara Findikoglu. Biopic when?

Edebiri wears (from left): Conner Ives; Giovanna Flores; vintage tee, Still Kelly pants, Chanel bag.

Why this was her year: Post-Bear, trying newly introduced things with her career (Broadway; Woolf), and her fashion (Giovanna Flores patchwork dress; Chanel tail feathers).

Best look of 2026: She showed the boys how it’s done in a slick Conner Ives suit.

Schafer wears (from left): Prada; Gimaguas dress; Celine.

Best off-duty look of 2026: The silky purple backward button-up over a tomato-red Gimaguas minidress she wore down the Chateau Marmont driveway.

Her style, in essence: Up for anything, from Gustav Klimt’s Mäda Primavesi to dystopian fembot.

Abrams wears (from left): Balenciaga by Nicolas Ghesquière top, Hamish Olrik pants, Chanel shoes; Colleen Allen; vintage tee from Moth Food, Chanel pants, shoes, and bag.

Best off-duty look of 2026: The sporty, vintage-looking “Vote” baseball tee paired with high-waisted wool trousers and Chanel’s signature cap-toe shoes: effortless, elegant, utterly cool.

MVPs and benchwarmers alike stole the show with their ’fits this year.

Osaka wears Miss Claire Sullivan; Hana Yagi.

Why 2026 was her year: The four-time Grand Slam champ reached her first-ever Wimbledon quarterfinal and went all-in on her fashion, on and off the court.

Her slam-dunk look: Acing Wimbledon whites in a Hana Yagi walkout look inspired by traditional Japanese ceremonial attire.

Clarkson wears (from left): Abercrombie & Fitch; vintage T-shirt, Louis Vuitton scarf, Hat Club hat; Chrome Hearts jacket, Saint Laurent pants.

Why 2026 was his year: Knicks in 5.

His slam-dunk look: A fitted black Rick Owens long-sleeve and pants amidst the Paris heatwave. He ditched the shirt post-show—not that we’re complaining.

Why 2026 was his year: A ruptured Achilles and dashed World Cup dreams didn’t keep the French footballer from Wimbledon or the Balenciaga front row.

His slam-dunk look: A Miu Miu Canadian tuxedo, vested for maximum bicep-baring.

They are not like other guys, in that you’ll never catch them in a snoozy black tux.

O’Connor wears (from left): Lemaire; vintage jacket, Adidas track pants; Hermès.

Best look of 2026: The all-black Hermès leather shirt-and-trousers ensemble that gagged the internet.

Why we can’t get enough: The swerve from tweedy London boy to louche fashion lad. We always knew he had it in him.

Why this was his year: Euphoria, Disclosure Day, and Michael (plus an Emmy nomination for The Four Seasons); shutting down every single step-and-repeat along the way.

Best outfit of 2026: The custom purple caped Valentino look dotted with Boucheron jewels was the antidote to the standard-glitch suit.

Innanen wears (from left): a vintage tee, Jeanerica jeans, Loewe bag; 6397 shirt and pants, Sena loafers, Aaron Levine bag; vintage tee, Jeanerica jeans, Dunst jacket.

Why 2026 was his year: From season 2 of Adults to the front rows of Paris Fashion Week, Innanen reminded us that he is far more than just a TikTok star.

Why we can’t get enough: On one Fresh York City scorcher, he made it clear he was in heat in a Horny graphic tee.

Malkovich wears (from left): Dior; Chanel; Aubero.

Why 2026 was his year: Malkovich has always been a bona fide fashion obsessive (lest we forget his past ventures in menswear design as “Technobohemian”). Wild Horse Nine gave him the red carpets to prove it.

Breakout moment of 2026: The Dior suit with a ruff collar he wore at the Venice Film Festival was a cross between a Tudor courtier and frill-necked lizard.

They’re your favorite fashion editor’s favorite fashion editor…and stylist and buyer and model.

Recent findings suggest that on Marci: JW Anderson shirt, Ruadh jeans, Loewe bag. On Lori: Nahmias shirt, Chanel skirt, Alaïa bag.

Why the fashion industry loves them: No one inspires envy as consistently as aunt-niece duo Lori and Marci Hirshleifer, who operate the dynastic Manhasset store Hirshleifers.

Why 2026 was their year: At a time when everyone is looking to amp up their personal style, these two have it in spades.

Bellizzi wears (from left): Dior by John Galliano; Chanel; Versace.

Why 2026 was her year: After receiving an Oscar nomination for her work on Marty Supreme, Bellizzi styled her first Vogue shoot and pulled double duty at 6397’s spring 2027 show, both styling and walking in it.

Highlight reel: Galliano Dior, Blazy Chanel, Dario Versace.

Lebasi in Miss Claire Sullivan.

Why 2026 was her year: When she isn’t styling Vogue Italia shoots or walking the Conner Ives runway, Lebasi consults for CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund finalist Miss Claire Sullivan.

Best outfit: At the 2026 CFDA Fashion Fund Finalist cocktail, Lebasi elevated a white tee and blue jeans with a Miss Claire Sullivan bolero. Someone’s already got the 2027 Met Gala theme down.

According to recent reports, left: Rick Owens jacket, Afghani embroidered chapan, Sea trousers, Kero shoes, COS cummerbund, Chimi sunglasses. Right: Miu Miu pants and shoes, Prada button-up, Calvin Klein bra, Gentle Monster sunglasses.

Why this was her year: At the spring 2027 collections, the Swedish-Pakistani catwalker seemed to open (Fendi, Victoria Beckham, Sacai) or close (Tom Ford, Hermès, Louis Vuitton) every show that mattered.

Her best look: The teeny tank top and hip-slung jeans she was spotted wearing off-runway at Paris Fashion Week would get a nod of approval from Haider Ackermann, who put her in the season’s most barely-there bathing suit at Tom Ford.

In a recent development, left: Ojuromi. Center: Ojuromi wears a dress by Debby Fasingha. Right: Fasingha.

Why the fashion industry loves them: This duo grew their homespun, high-energy Lagos fashion showcases into a global sensation. Through Ojuromi and Fasingha’s lens, fashion feels fresh, personal, and full of possibility.

Why 2026 was their year: After a video of Ojuromi walking in Fasingha’s DIY, Chanel-inspired looks went viral, the model made her runway debut at the brand’s spring 2027 show.

Louisa Jacobson’s Stylist on 10 Things That Inspire Her Red Carpet Looks

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1382 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in fashion, anything from niche archival research to a favorite film to an outfit you saw on your morning commute can make for inspiration.
  • Method dressing has become the road most traveled for Hollywood A-listers and their stylists.
  • Recent findings suggest that “One thing that we are always aware of is not being the character she plays on TV, because she is more than that,” Jacobson’s stylist Edward Bowleg III told Harper’s Bazaar over Zoom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in fashion, anything from niche archival research to a favorite film to an outfit you saw on your morning commute can make for inspiration. In our upcoming series 10 Things, we ask industry professionals and tastemakers to divulge the (you guessed it) 10 things that had the most impact on their aesthetic choices.

Method dressing has become the road most traveled for Hollywood A-listers and their stylists. We’ve seen Zendaya and Law Roach turn out goddess-like dresses in homage to the actress’s role of Athena in The Odyssey, while the cast of the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping has been channeling their outlandish onscreen personas into equally over-the-top red carpet looks. But even though period pieces present a prime opportunity for imitation, The Gilded Age star Louisa Jacobson, who plays Marian Brook in the Julian Fellowes series, says she’d rather dress like herself.

Recent findings suggest that “One thing that we are always aware of is not being the character she plays on TV, because she is more than that,” Jacobson’s stylist Edward Bowleg III told Harper’s Bazaar over Zoom. “She is a fully fleshed-out human being. She is Louisa and she is not Marian. That is an important distinction.”.

In a recent development, bowleg started working with the actress in 2022 after a mutual friend introduced them right around the time that The Gilded Age was set to premiere. The editorial stylist, who has worked for countless publications and brands like Hermès, Valentino, and Marc Jacobs, recalls his first official project with Jacobson: the 2022 Vanity Fair Oscars party, to which she wore an ivory off-the-shoulder Khaite gown with a Jeffrey Levinson clutch.

Much has changed in the four years since that evening. “When she cut her hair short, that was the moment where a lot shifted,” said Bowleg. “It was a upcoming her.” With the fresh haircut came a slew of delightfully unexpected red carpet moments, spanning a handful of tailored suits (and a cummerbund!) from Haider Ackermann’s Tom Ford, Conner Ives, and Calvin Klein Collection to a Dilara Findikoglu minidress with an armored bodice made from safety pins, metal accents, and a tattered chiffon train.

According to recent reports, jacobson’s fashion evolution paralleled her own self-actualization. “Exploring sexual identity and being more free with that led to having more fun with experimental fashion and being unapologetic about what she likes and who she is,” stated Bowleg. And it highlights: She’s been on a winning style streak recently.

Coming off Jacobson’s recent Gilded Age press tour, which saw looks from Haider Ackermann’s Tom Ford, Ashlyn, Commission, and Mel Usine, Bowleg sat down with Bazaar to decode 10 influences that shaped his fashion choices, from Saint Laurent’s le smoking to an Azzedine Alaïa collection that lives rent-free in his head.

“We love tailoring, we love a suit. I could have her in a suit every day of the week. She went to her first Tom Ford show in March. When she told me she was invited, I was like ‘Oh my god, that is so cool,’ because I am a big fan. The 1996 Gucci show is burned into my brain. That is when my interest in fashion really began, so for me in a weird way it was almost like a full circle moment.

“I think with creative director Haider Ackermann’s tailoring in particular, the cut is so exquisite. When we have fittings with them, the only thing we are adjusting is the length of the trousers. There is also a confidence that she has when she puts them on. It’s very commanding. Then you mix that in with all of the elements—there is always a really sexy shoe that goes along with it.”.

According to recent reports, “An image that could have been on the moodboard would be Helmut Newton’s photos of Saint Laurent’s Le Smoking with the women on the street in Paris. There is one image with a naked woman wearing just heels, standing with another woman in Le Smoking. That is very much the kind of vibe we are going for: mixing something sexy and feminine with tailoring, which is inherently masculine.”.

“She went to the Met Gala this year with Dilara [Findikoglu]. When I had the conversation with Dilara and her team, the idea of armor came up. She had been to the Met ahead of our conversation, and she sent me all of these pictures that she had taken in the Medieval section where they have the helmets and the chain mail and the body armor. Those were just things that she loved and that became a massive inspiration for the look.”.

Industry observers note that “For Louisa’s first Met Gala in 2022 (the red carpet theme was ‘Gilded Glamour, White Tie’) there was a John Singer Sargent painting of a woman in a black dress. The image helped direct our choice of look”—a futuristic gown with a gold trompe l'œil skeleton molded in leather and hand-painted in gold leaf from the Schiaparelli Spring/Summer 2022 Haute Couture collection by Daniel Roseberry.

“I love Azzedine Alaïa. Specifically the 1986 show—the one with all of the bandage dressing with the cut-outs on the sides and the infamous denim and leather zip that goes all across the body. I believe Grace Jones walked. Even with the McQueen that she just wore, in a way it’s that sort of vibe—the bomber jacket but with the little skirt. It’s that kind of energy: A strong, powerful woman.”.

“There has been quite a bit of leather. The McQueen that she just wore, the Khaite full leather suit that she wore to the Vanity Fair Oscars party. She put it on, and it was like ‘This is fab.’ We were wondering if it was right for Vanity Fair and whether she would be the only one in a suit. I told Louisa that Zendaya had worn a suit the year before and I also was kind of like, ‘Fuck it, you look hot, this is great.’ Then there were two more leather Louis Vuitton looks that she wore. One was to the Vanity Fair Oscars party in 2024. And then before that, she wore a Vuitton look to the SAG Awards and the whole bodice was sculpted in leather, as well.”.

“Hedi Slimane is a big inspiration of mine. Again, it’s a lot of tailoring, it’s leather, it’s a great silhouette. It’s the aesthetic overall, but in particular, it was the fall/winter 2006 collection that he did. There were things that were skinny and then there were things that were a bit more loose in terms of the trousers. There was a softness to the hardness of it all. It was still very edgy and a bit rock ‘n’ roll, but there was a soft glamour to it. That is something that I like with Louisa, even when it comes to the jewelry.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I am really curious to see what Pieter Mulier will do with Versace and Atelier Versace is in January. [I should also say that] I am obsessed with Donatella Versace. When I started looking at all things [high] fashion, Donatella was another designer that I loved. That glamour and excess and sexiness—she is unapologetically who she is.”.

According to recent reports, “With music and ‘90s hip-hop, you look at the bling, the diamonds, and things like that. I love a great jewelry moment, so accessorizing Louisa’s looks with the right jewelry is always important part to me. I love diamonds. When she recently went to a Tiffany & Co. event [in Ashlyn], we initially had our brooch up on the lapel where you would traditionally see it. Then she was like, ‘It doesn’t feel right.’ So I moved it down to the peplum of the jacket. It was a substantial, big yellow diamond, which I was obsessed with. I just loved how much it sparkled and shined.”.

“Helmut Lang is also a significant inspiration. There is a Spring 1998 men's collection and a Spring 1999 collection that I think about a lot in terms of silhouette and things that still resonate today. It all comes from having researched some of those collections in the past, so they tend to be recurring elements in the work.”.

It’s what our family reaches for whenever we need a simple, nourishing dish that warms from the inside out. For the smoothest porridge, let the rice soak in cold water before cooking.

Recent findings suggest that if you have time, soak the rice, which makes the texture softer and can aid in digestion. Place washed rice in a bowl and pour in water to cover by 1". Soak at least 30 minutes and up to 4 hours. Drain off excess water before starting the recipe. The wakame seaweed, which you’ve probably had in miso soup, can typically be found dried anywhere Asian groceries are available.

In The Fourth Trimester, we ask parents: What meal nourished you after welcoming your baby? This month it’s a cozy rice porridge by Eating at Home cookbook author Trinity Mouzon Wofford. Read more: Breakfast at Home, After Birth at Home.

In a recent development, combine 1 cup short-grain rice, washed, soaked if desired, ¼ cup dried wakame (seaweed), 1 Tbsp. dried red shiso, and 6 cups low-sodium broth (any kind) or water in a large donabe, medium Dutch oven, or other heavy pot. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat (you’ll hear bubbling). Uncover and stir, making sure nothing is stuck to bottom of pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Continue to cook porridge 30 minutes more (resist the urge to peek).

According to recent reports, remove pot from heat and let porridge sit (still covered) 10 minutes. Uncover and stir. Rice grains should be cooked through, broken open, and creamy, but porridge should still be fairly loose. Season porridge with fine sea salt.

Ladle porridge into bowls and serve, topped with toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, and/or thinly sliced scallions.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You have a keen eye for a fashionable investment—whether it’s a vintage accessory, a high-quality classic, or a trendy piece to keep your wardrobe current. But your closet isn’t the only arena that’s kept up to date. With your finger on the pulse of all things elegant and practical, no doubt the latest and greatest in personal transportation—electric cars—is firmly on your radar. This automotive upgrade is a step toward the future, and, like all newly introduced things, comes with some specific guidelines. With the help of State Farm, we’ve outlined what to consider before you elevate your status to EV owner—from how the flexibility of an EV factors into your routine, travel aims, and commute to how best to protect your fabulous new asset.

When choosing an EV, consider how it fits into your lifestyle. Location, budget, and driving habits should all play a role in finding the right fit. For example, if you spend a lot of time on the highway, a hybrid may make more sense than an all-electric model since you’ll have gas as a backup when your battery runs low. You’ll also want to think about how much passenger and cargo space you need—if you’re regularly hauling people, pets, or plenty of (literal) baggage, compare the costs of larger models that can accommodate everything comfortably.

You love vintage, but does that extend to your car? It just depends on your needs.

In a recent development, when deciding to buy pre-owned or new, think about how long you’re looking to own the car. Consider battery wear and how much it costs to replace one, your total budget (including financing, maintenance, and insurance), and whether or not you’re eligible for any tax credits that could offset the price of a new EV.

Yes, you’re already envisioning yourself pulling onto the street in your fabulous latest ride, but make sure you weigh the pros and cons to save yourself from buyer’s remorse later.

Sources indicate that you passionately curate your life, and the same should go for your electric car’s coverage. When considering insurance, EVs require a bit of what non-electric cars need, along with a few additional protections.

Protecting yourself and your investment starts with liability, collision, and comprehensive, just like with traditional cars. But with an EV, you’ll also need to cover battery damage, charging equipment, and specialized repairs. As a result—and because of higher purchase prices, specialized parts and repairs, and more—pricing tends to be higher than on policies for traditional cars. Manage these costs by comparing quotes on the model you choose, taking advantage of discounts for anti-theft devices and safe driving records, and, if you can help manage the potential out-of-pocket cost, adjusting your deductible a bit higher to lower your monthly payments.

Recent findings suggest that you don’t need to do this all alone, though. Just like you’d turn to a trusted friend for a second opinion on your outfit, State Farm is there to answer your EV insurance questions and offer you an insurance quote before you buy.

Industry observers note that when shopping for an EV, think about how far you’ll typically drive, where you’ll charge, and how long charging will take. Most EVs can go around 200 miles on a full charge at lower city speeds, but your charging setup matters, too. If you’re planning to charge at home, you’ll want to factor in installation of a charger, electricity costs, and potential homeowners insurance considerations. If you’ll rely on public chargers, make sure there’s a reliable network along your usual routes. It’s also worth knowing what kind of charger your car uses: Level 1 chargers plug into a standard outlet and can take up to 24 hours, while Level 2 chargers use a 240-volt outlet and offer a faster, more convenient option for home charging.

Much like you carry a purse-sized mending kit for fashion fixes, it’s always good to have an EV backup plan for automotive emergencies.

Add EV-specific roadside assistance to your insurance plan.

Collision or comprehensive insurance could cover this, or your warranty may cover normal degradation.

After your deductible payment, collision or comprehensive coverage should help lower costs.

The answer varies by model, so do your research, but know that you can add gap insurance or upcoming car replacement to your initiative to mitigate the concern.

This marked his third victory in Vegas and his 75th top-spot finish at a Grand Prix, and he bested Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, who came in second and third, respectively.

Sources indicate that each year, numerous F1 Grand Prix races are held around the world, with 22 events set to take place in 2026, ending with the circuit in Abu Dhabi in December. (There were originally 24 on the calendar, but the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix were canceled back in April.).

But, while there are quite a few Grand Prix to enjoy all year long, the Las Vegas races always bring out some of the starriest names, and this year was no exception.

From the stands, F1 regulars like Keanu Reeves and Kim Kardashian took it all in, with the latter there to cheer on her boyfriend, Lewis Hamilton (who finished 7th for Ferrari). Meanwhile, other A-listers in attendance included Lisa, Teyana Taylor, Venus Williams, Sarah Michelle Gellar, Nina Dobrev, Rachel Brosnahan, and Eiza González, who moved between qualifiers, races, parties, and more.

Apple Juice Bread

📅 22 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level.
  • Sources indicate that I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal.
  • Industry observers note that take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level. The subtle, but unmistakable, undercurrent of apple sweetness struck me as a bit of a magic trick in a bread that, otherwise, to the eye and hand was just a soft white loaf.

Sources indicate that I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal. When I asked him what he did differently to prepare it, he said he just took the same rustic bread recipe he baked elsewhere and used apple juice in place of water. I was incredulous. That was it? The same amount? The same technique? Yes and yes, he said. I was hooked. It turns out the water-to-juice switcheroo gives an added taste of fall without taking anything away from the shape and texture. It’s become an instant favorite at my house both breakfast and lunch, and I expect it will be at yours.

Industry observers note that take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed. You can do it!

More apple recipes here: 37 Apple Desserts That Make Us Want to Pick the Whole Orchard.

Mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

Sources indicate that set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold. Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

In a recent development, transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

Sources indicate that place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center. Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.) Working very swiftly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

Sources indicate that bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing.

Do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.

#100877. The Under-The-Radar Brands the Best Dressed List Loved in 2026

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1912 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vogue ↗ Open Full Page

The Under-The-Radar Brands the Best Dressed List Loved in 2026

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1912 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that vogue’s 2026 best dressed list certainly knows its way around a luxury label ambassadorship: Chanel swans, Saint Laurent savants, Dior devotees, Miu Miu girls and Prada protégés.
  • In a recent development, the distinction between under-the-radar and fashion-crowd famous is becoming increasingly blurred.
  • Greta Lee, Hunter Schafer, and Whitney Peak have embraced the retro-futurist designs of Zane Li’s Lii, the award-winning label crafted from his unassuming and tiny Chinatown studio.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that vogue’s 2026 best dressed list certainly knows its way around a luxury label ambassadorship: Chanel swans, Saint Laurent savants, Dior devotees, Miu Miu girls and Prada protégés. But along the way, you’ll find that some of this year’s most thrilling moments for ‘stepping out’ and ‘stunning’ (as per the celebrity style news cycle) came courtesy of designers whose names aren’t quite so familiar. For this particularly discerning crowd, an emerging designer and an IYKYK label carries just a bit more sartorial currency.

In a recent development, the distinction between under-the-radar and fashion-crowd famous is becoming increasingly blurred. Designers like Conner Ives and Rachel Scott’s Diotima have developed considerable celebrity followings and their fair share of viral moments, while labels like Kallmeyer are hardly insider secrets anymore. The next generation, however, is hot on their heels.

Greta Lee, Hunter Schafer, and Whitney Peak have embraced the retro-futurist designs of Zane Li’s Lii, the award-winning label crafted from his unassuming and tiny Chinatown studio. Tessa Thompson, Ayo Edebiri, and Paloma Elsesser, meanwhile, found plenty to love in Giovanna Flores’s free-form silhouettes, pattern agnosticism, and deadstock materials. Elsewhere, Elle Fanning indulged in the character play of August Barron, Jenna Ortega put a young designer’s extraordinary corsetry craftsmanship on the red carpet, and John Malkovich looked to upcycled lace. Rosalía has made something of a habit of championing emerging talent, with the likes of Yasmina Atta and Laura Andraschko finding a place in her expansive, prima ballerina meets bad-girl Mary Magdalene wardrobe.

It has been revealed that more than a passing fascination with the next substantial thing, this year’s best dressed list has fostered relationships with designers in ways that speak to their genuine curiosity and enthusiasm about clothes, the people making them, and the exciting places fashion is heading. Below, the under-the-radar brands this year’s best dressed loved.

Greta lee wears Giovanna Flores.

Brooklyn-based Giovanna Flores is a fast favorite among Hollywood’s most adventurous dressers for her scavenger-chic designs. Her work is often made using deadstock and recycled textiles, and utilizes unexpected fabric combinations, patchworking, and inventive draping. Paloma Elsesser dropped her polka dot bodice and zebra-hemmed G.F. fit amid one fab Instagram dump, and Tessa Thompson mixed her prints with a sumptuous Bordeaux sash. Ayo Edebiri opted for a mismatched strawberry seed and gingham number, while Greta Lee wore some canary yellow velvet. (Both Edebiri and Lee are styled by Danielle Goldberg and hold Chanel and Dior ambassador titles respectively—Flores’s spliced-and-diced one-of-ones are a must-have.).

In a recent development, zane Li’s Lii is a fashion-crowd secret hiding in plain sight; this year, he netted the LVMH Karl Lagerfeld Prize for Innovation and was a CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund winner. Known for its architectural minimalism and precise construction in enchanting color combos, the Newly introduced York label has struck a major chord. Greta Lee, again, was an early champion, most recently wearing an architectural two-toned blue dress with a sexy thigh-high slit. Whitney Peak wore a twisted tank and skirt look fresh from the spring 2027 runway—a collection that unspooled the emotional threads between girlhood and womanhood, reflected in dramatically skewed tops and miniskirts in scuba materials and wide-eyed shades of teal and tomato. Hunter Schafer has incorporated the retro-futurist designs into her ongoing Blade Runner 2099 press tour. Consider Lii a modern fixture in the wardrobes of Hollywood’s experimental minimalists.

Another Yasmina Atta custom design.

Rosalía has spent the last year either en pointe or expounding the possibilities of a popstar’s wardrobe, oscillating between the ecclesiastical and the balletic. London-based, Nigerian-born designer Yasmina Atta, a Central Saint Martins graduate whose surrealist designs draw on African cinema, folklore, and subculture, was central to one of Rosalía’s most viral fashion moments. This was when she stepped out in New York in a custom Atta creation: a plunging, sheer bronze latex bodice, visible black lace lingerie, a dramatically dropped waist, and a frothy cream tutu, all cinched with studded belts—a look partly inspired by Edgar Degas’s Little Dancer Aged Fourteen. (Rosalía had also worn a slate-gray wool minidress by the designer earlier in the year.) For a musician whose Lux era has been defined by religious iconography and the discipline of dance, Atta’s fantastical yet fervent approach to fashion is a perfect fit.

Rosalia wears Laura Andraschko.

Laura Andraschko’s hedonistic, subculture-informed designs also found a fan in Rosalía. The Berlin- and Vienna-raised Central Saint Martins graduate draws on various influences: indie sleaze and nightlife, aristocrats, Sloane Rangers, and Alpine bunny glam. Rosalía has worn the designer on several occasions: at the 2026 US Open, she chose an Andraschko T-shirt, while a previous Paris outing saw her in a khaki minidress from the fall 2025 Après Ski collection, with a dramatic furry hem and velvet-trimmed, off-the-shoulder neckline. More recently, of course, she had to pull on a tutu-like skirt. It’s feminine and anarchic and exactly right for Rosalía.

Jenna Ortega wears Elias Matso.

Recent findings suggest that jenna Ortega and her stylist Enrique Melendez spent last year crafting a deviant glam-goth wardrobe for the Wednesday star. This year, we’ve witnessed a subtle evolution into freer experiments with color and textiles. For a Newly introduced York screening of Klara and the Sun, Ortega wore a sculptural creation by young designer Elias Matso, made from steel corset boning and 6,500 beads, all inspired by the colors of painter Marc Ranger. The Polimoda graduate’s approach to corsetry is theatrical and technically audacious, with references ranging from Bob Mackie to Charles James. The custom dress reportedly took more than 300 hours to make, and marked a major red carpet moment for a designer early in his career.

In a recent development, “This dress was a massive test of my free will and just how much I was willing to put towards something that did not have a guaranteed return,” Matso said. “It was scary, I felt crazy at times, I lost a lot of money, and now this object exists. After many blisters, rebuilds, failed trials, international shipping nightmares, and working on it in six different cities with so many helping hands it just exists, and that is wild.” A hand-crafting corsetier to know.

Elle Fanning wears August Barron.

It has been revealed that elle Fanning is all about the Effie-coded whimsy right now, and Paris-based August Barron has proven a kindred spirit in this quest. Formerly known as All-In, the label is the brainchild of Benjamin Barron and Bror August Vestbø, whose designs play with heady ideas of domesticity, nostalgia, and the conventions of femininity. Fanning made a memorable appearance in a pale yellow striped polo shirt and a voluminous, bow-adorned tulle skirt from their fall 2026 Bedtime Story collection. The design duo has a talent for taking familiar clothes and articulating something thrilling throught them. Whether referencing American pageant girls, cabaret queens, housewives, gay icons Judy or a Marilyn, August Barron provides the much-needed glitch in the glamour for those brave enough to dial in.

London-based GOYAGOMA was the talk of London Fashion Week when the label made its debut earlier this year at designer incubator Fashion East (the same one that birthed Simone Rocha, Martine Rose, and Grace Wales Bonner.) Of course, Paloma Elsesser picked up his designs fast, and previous best dressed honoree A$AP Rocky is a fan. Founded by Bahamian designer Traiceline Pratt, a Central Saint Martins graduate who previously worked with Phoebe Philo and A-Cold-Wall, the label draws on memories of growing up in the Bahamas to reimagine everyday clothing through luxe fabrications, exaggerated proportions, and determined tailoring. Elsesser’s endorsement adds to an already growing list of admirers of the designer’s assuredly off-beat approach to the capsule wardrobe—expect to see it hit Dover Street Market soon, too.

Julie Kegels takes her bow during spring 2027.

According to recent reports, antwerp-born Julie Kegels has established herself as one of the most interrogative young voices in European fashion, and both Paloma Elsesser and Rosalia have taken notice. A graduate of Antwerp’s Royal Academy of Fine Arts who went on to work at Alaïa, Kegels launched her namesake label in 2024, exploring the tension between conventional feminine dressing and something more surreal. Her collections manipulate familiar silhouettes through draping and distortion, taking as much inspiration from working girls as she does from furniture. Winning the 2026 LVMH Prize has only accelerated her ascent—her signature thong socks are an even speedier way into the brand, or you could hold out for her aims to invest her LVMH prize money into the development of more shoes and bags.

Miyako Bellizzi styled and walked the spring 2027 show.

Sarah Pidgeon during a 6397 fitting.

Founded by Stella Ishii in 2013, with Lizzie Owens now leading design, Upcoming York label 6397 has built a quietly influential universe of lived-in separates and pieces that slyly riff on what “staples” can mean. Among its fans are Paloma Elsesser, Greta Lee, and Sarah Pidgeon. The brand’s debut runway show was styled by costume designer and best dressed lister Miyako Bellizzi, who also walked in the presentation. The downtown creative community has long embraced 6397, and this is the New York woman energy you just want to bottle.

Whitney Peak wears spring 2026, styled by Karla Welch.

London-based Torishéju takes an experimental and emotive approach to pattern-cutting and construction: trained as a menswear designer, Torishéju Dumi has built a sartorial world that plays with trompe l’oeil and other-century costuming made modern, combining subversive design twists and classic craft techniques. Whitney Peak, on The Hunger Games press tour, opted for a deconstructed scarlet red leather skirt brought together by sensual draping and thigh-high cutouts, paired with a sculpted black halter top. This is the one for those who like their fashion with a little friction.

Ayo Edebiri wears Still Kelly pants.

Never underestimate the power of a great pair of trousers. And as Ayo Edebiri knows, the best off-duty outfits often hinge on an immaculate basic. Her choice? Still Kelly’s tailored black trousers worn with a vintage Björk T-shirt sourced by stylist Danielle Goldberg. The brand describes itself as a sartorial “slow burn.” “Building a world, making good products, it takes time,” founder Marc Kalman previously told Vogue. “I’m cool with that.”.

Louisa Jacobson wears Catalogue NYC.

Louisa Jacobson has never been one for fashion’s binaries. With stylist Edward Bowleg III, she delights in the push-and-pull of buttoned-up tailoring and daring exposure, masculine codes and feminine flourishes. Catalogue NYC is exactly the sort of emerging designer label that articulates that. Founded by former Peter Do designers Pablo Correa and An Nguyen alongside Vincent Ho, the New York brand approaches familiar wardrobe pieces with an experimental eye, proposing new ways of wearing tailoring and dresses. On Jacobson, those ideas find an exquisite home.

Industry observers note that A saucy sliver of toe and a beckoning, warped heel have become immediately identifiable Jude signatures. The Paris-based footwear label was founded in 2024 by Jurgita Dileviciute and Denitsa Bumbarova, and the duo’s subtly subversive designs take familiar shoe silhouettes and give them a deliciously peculiar twist—most notably with their barely-there peep toes. Zoë Kravitz is a fan of the Date pump, while Sarah Pidgeon favors the Date mule. Tracee Ellis Ross has amassed a well-curated collection of Jude footwear, from the sinuous Fame pump to the Haze sandal. It’s little wonder the label has found favor with fashion’s freakiest feet: Jude knows that even the smallest detail can demand a double take at the dogs.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The announcement comes nearly three months after Grande concluded her first concert tour in seven years, an experience she has previously described as a significant chapter in her career.
  • Here’s everything we know about the project so far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ariana Grande’s Eternal Sunshine Tour may have wrapped in September, but fans will soon get another chance to experience it. On November 23, the singer shared a video teasing an upcoming concert film documenting the tour, which is set to premiere on Peacock.

The announcement comes nearly three months after Grande concluded her first concert tour in seven years, an experience she has previously described as a significant chapter in her career.

Here’s everything we know about the project so far.

Grande has yet to share specific details about the project, including whether it will feature a complete concert performance, behind-the-scenes footage, or a combination of both.

Her Eternal Sunshine Tour began in Oakland, California, on June 6 and concluded on September 1 following 10 performances at London’s O2 Arena. The shows featured music from across her discography, including Eternal Sunshine, Positions, and her latest album, Petal, which was released in July.

The tour also marked Grande’s return to the concert stage following her 2019 Sweetener World Tour. Throughout the run, she performed in custom looks from designers including Alexander McQueen, Givenchy, and Vivienne Westwood, styled by Law Roach.

Grande shared the first teaser on Instagram on November 23, in collaboration with Peacock and Team Ariana.

Recent findings suggest that the video features footage of Grande performing the title track from Eternal Sunshine. As the performance ends, the screen reveals the message: “Coming soon to… Peacock.”.

During an August interview with Vosk in the City, Grande reflected on how her latest tour differed from her previous experiences performing live.

“I think my last tour I wasn’t necessarily in the same place in life, and I wasn’t able to be as present as I am this time,” she explained, describing the Eternal Sunshine Tour as “such a beautiful corrective experience.”.

Grande also spoke about reconnecting with longtime fans through songs spanning more than a decade of her career.

According to recent reports, in August, her representative confirmed that the singer planned to step away from public-facing work following the tour. Grande later addressed the decision during a concert in Chicago, explaining that it had been made well in advance.

“It is something that I have decided; it’s a plan that I had quietly made a long time ago, and it’s a decision that was made from a thoughtful and empowered place,” she told the audience.

Sources indicate that an official release date has yet to be unveiled. For now, Grande’s teaser only confirms that the film is coming soon to Peacock.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, while scrolling through my Instagram feed last week, I came across a pair of T-shirts made by Sofia Coppola for Mack Books. To celebrate the release of her mother Eleanor’s documentary, Making Marie Antoinette—a portrait compiled from archival footage shot during the making of Coppola’s 2006 cult classic—as well as the original film’s 20th anniversary, Coppola has released a limited-edition capsule collection printed with on-set photography by Andrew Durham. Naturally, I had a T-shirt in my basket faster than you could say “Let them eat cake.” (In case you were wondering, I went for the one with Kirsten Dunst looking wistfully out from a rococo horse-drawn carriage, a camera rig looming in the foreground.).

But it also got me thinking, not for the first time, about film directors and fashion. There’s a reason why the behind-the-scenes photos from that movie—Dunst and Jason Schwartzman in powdered wigs and full Versailles regalia listening to their iPods, Coppola crouched behind a monitor in a button-down and jeans; you know the ones—have remained such an enduring touchstone within the online cultural consciousness, from Tumblr to TikTok. There’s something both fascinating and lightly absurd about the friction between the practical, gorpy clothing worn by most on a film set and the breathtaking opulence of the period costuming. And in Making Marie Antoinette, Coppola’s casual but stylish on-set wardrobe of well-cut mid-aughts basics is, counterintuitively, almost as captivating as Milena Canonero’s glorious 18th-century costume confections. Which I guess is partly why Coppola made those T-shirts.

It has been revealed that but it’s also partly why the best directors—those who spend their lives building worlds and poring over the details of what their character might say, do, and, most importantly for our purposes, wear—have become as compelling to watch on the red carpet as the contract-bound movie stars they direct. (It’s little wonder that some of history’s greatest filmmakers were also some of history’s most stylish, possessing an innate understanding of the storytelling power of clothes: Agnès Varda, David Lynch, Wong Kar-wai, the list goes on.).

Which brings me to the 2026 awards trail—and the 2027 awards trail, which is now kicking into gear—where the sartorial approaches have been refreshingly eclectic. While promoting Sinners, Ryan Coogler’s killer red carpet looks included a three-piece Thom Browne suit with a diamond brooch at the Golden Globes, a slouchy Fear of God suit at the SAG Awards, and a sharp Louis Vuitton tux at the Oscars.

Ryan Coogler (with his wife, Zinzi) in Thom Browne at the Golden Globes.

Coogler in Louis Vuitton at the Oscars.

For Chloé Zhao—who, not coincidentally, earned a spot on this year’s Vogue best dressed list—campaigning for Hamnet appeared to involve taking cues from the world of her film. (Turns out directors can do method dressing too.) Working with Gabriela Hearst, she wore a gold gown with a Tudor-inflected Basque waist at the BAFTAs, while at the Academy Awards, she wore a headline-grabbing gown inspired by Victorian mourning dress—complete with draped bell sleeves, Bulgari diamonds, and a sheer black veil—that she described as “the alchemical image of the crow.” Try getting that level of commitment from a leading man in a black tux and a brand-deal watch.

Chloé Zhao in Gabriela Hearst at the BAFTAs.

Zhao in Gabriela Hearst at the Oscars.

Recent findings suggest that thankfully, this year, there’s a new crop of fashion-fluent directors ready to take up the mantle. Just take Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, known collectively as Los Javis, who have happily matched the maximalist, operatic sweep of their Lorca-inspired epic La Bola Negra with their steady stream of playful tailoring—coordinating Loewe suits at the Biarritz Film Festival, say, or oversized shirting and denim to the Chanel show over the summer—proving their flair for the visual extends well beyond the silver screen.

Los Javis—or Javi Ambrossi and Javi Calvo—at the GQ Men of the Year Awards in Madrid.

Ambrossi and Calvo in Chanel at the brand’s haute couture fall 2026 show.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Olivia Wilde has been delivering some of the year’s sharpest high-low looks while promoting The Invite—everything from a custom Saint Laurent dress with an ab-baring cutout at the Los Angeles premiere, to a boxy black vintage tee and double-pleated pants from The Row for a SAG-AFTRA event. “I really love not having to dress up in the same way as I have as an actress,” she told Chloe Malle on the Vogue podcast earlier this year. “I do feel like after decades of tarting myself up for press tours, I am so relieved to be like, ‘You know what? They wear T-shirts. I’m gonna wear a fucking T-shirt.’” (Granted, wearing a T-shirt hits a little differently when it’s tucked into pants that cost roughly the same as a secondhand Honda Civic, but the point stands.).

Olivia Wilde in Saint Laurent at The Invite’s Los Angeles premiere.

Wilde in a vintage x Karla tee and The Row pants at a SAG-AFTRA Foundation event.

Then, there’s Greta Gerwig, who’s gearing up for the February release of her rock-opera-inspired Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew, whose looks this year—Bottega Veneta, Stella McCartney, Diotima by Rachel Scott—hint at a bold (and largely female-designed) press tour wardrobe to come.

Greta Gerwig in Bottega Veneta at the PGA Awards.

Gerwig in Ashlyn at the opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art.

According to recent reports, and finally, for a new vanguard of filmmakers, the press tour has become a place to subvert the traditional codes of men’s tailoring. On that front, there’s Club Kid’s Jordan Firstman and the Bottega Veneta suit he wore for the Los Angeles premiere, with its oversized powder-pink collar peeking over the top of the lapels, or the Tom Ford by Haider Ackermann jacket for the New York premiere that featured a silk floral boutonnière with a flowing ribbon. Or Jane Schoenbrun, who debuted their queer slasher, Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma, in Cannes with a series of offbeat looks that included a particularly delightful puffball skirt suit with powder-blue tights and Mary Janes.

Jordan Firstman in Tom Ford by Haider Ackermann at the Fresh York premiere of Club Kid.

Jane Schoenbrun at the Cannes premiere of Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma.

Recent findings suggest that it helps, of course, that in 2026, the lines between luxury fashion houses and cinema have all but dissolved. Fashion is no longer just dressing actors and directors for the premiere, or awards show; it’s actively financing, producing, and inserting itself into their work. In September, Dior revealed a two-year creative partnership with A24 before doubling down just this week with a upcoming Sundance Institute fellowship supporting women filmmakers. The Anthony Vaccarello–founded Saint Laurent Productions has cemented itself as a Cannes and awards-season powerhouse, backing auteurs such as Jim Jarmusch and Claire Denis. And some designers are stepping into the film set trenches, too—most notably Jonathan Anderson, who followed up his work on Challengers and Queer by designing the costumes for Guadagnino’s hotly anticipated Silicon Valley satire Artificial.

Clothes maketh the man. All of these directors know that clothes maketh the character. So let’s hope that, this awards season, clothes continue to maketh the filmmaker, too—and if they ever run out of ideas, I’ve got a Marie Antoinette T-shirt they’re welcome to borrow.

How Am I Supposed to Survive the Apocalypse Without My Phone?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (626 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that anyone who’s ever been trapped on a stalled subway or a WiFi-less flight knows how screwed we might feel without access to our phones.
  • It has been revealed that many found their way to Nomad, a pocket-sized device created to aid in offline situations.
  • Elsewhere, there are emergency libraries that you can download to your existing computer, with offline chatbots that can tell you how to find clean water or start a fire: lastbook.org, which includes how-to videos; Survival LLM, which offers up information from the CDC and FEMA; and Project Nomad (different from Studner’s Nomad), from Chris Sherwood, a prominent YouTuber.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that anyone who’s ever been trapped on a stalled subway or a WiFi-less flight knows how screwed we might feel without access to our phones. Last week’s tech outages––first, a failure of Microsoft’s systems, then, a national grounding of flights, followed by problems from Charles Schwab to Apple iCloud––were a reminder of how fragile our digital infrastructure is, especially at the dawn of AI. Preppers on Reddit, better known for discussing generators and the storage of food, began talking about how to AI–apocalypse proof the devices we’re all so dependent on. “getting serious about my preps with all the cyber attacks going on,” one user wrote. “I work for a security tech giant so I get a front row seat to a lot of the chaos. I’m specifically prepping for prolonged loss of power.”.

It has been revealed that many found their way to Nomad, a pocket-sized device created to aid in offline situations. “I had huge, huge spikes in traffic,” remarked Jackson Studner, creator of Nomad and a student at Millersville University of Pennsylvania. (“I’m not a tech giant or a startup, just a college student who enjoys building useful things and sharing them,” Studner’s website reads.) With the help of his professors, he built Nomad to provide some entertainment on camping trips and cross-country trips with friends. They’d hit a dead zone, and realize they wanted to watch a movie, or run video game software. Nomad is a miniscule server with TV and films, the entire Wikipedia library, and portable Wi-Fi, and offline maps. “I really like the reliability aspect,” Studner tells me. “I like to own my stuff. It's kind of that simple.” He’s also added navigation for his fresh community preparing for the apocalypse (or at least a grid shutdown). “It will actually tell you how to go along the road, it can tell you how to walk there, it'll calculate times, that kind of stuff,” he said.

Elsewhere, there are emergency libraries that you can download to your existing computer, with offline chatbots that can tell you how to find clean water or start a fire: lastbook.org, which includes how-to videos; Survival LLM, which offers up information from the CDC and FEMA; and Project Nomad (different from Studner’s Nomad), from Chris Sherwood, a prominent YouTuber. Sherwood is best known for posting explainer videos showing viewers how to build their “homelabs”—personal, at-home computing devices—under the name Crosstalk Solutions.

Recent findings suggest that the interest in Project Nomad, Sherwood remarked, has been overwhelming. “It’s got over 40,000 stars on GitHub, which means that 40,000 people not only saw the project and were on the page, but they clicked the little button to favorite it. And I'm getting over 200,000 views on the website per month,” he said.

In a recent development, despite his new fans, Sherwood himself isn’t a prepper. He was inspired by the Information Technology Disaster Resource Center (ITDRC), a non-profit that goes into disasters and provides internet services when they are completely down. “I had the opportunity to go on deployment with [ITDRC] when Hurricane Ian came through, and I saw firsthand all these people that were offline. It was a disaster. Getting people back online was almost as important as the food and water supplies that were getting set up to help with the recovery,” he explained.

Studner wasn’t a prepper either–– at first. But since Nomad took off and he’s found himself in more “prepper” corners of the internet, his feelings have slightly changed. “It’s for peace of mind. I have my little go bag. I'm not too, too worried about it, but I like to know that if there ever was a real problem, I'd be okay in that situation.”.

#100872. Industry News: Best Cutting Boards for Slicing, Dicing, and Chopping (2026)
